clue.text: Lakeside parking provided for stars …

parts.note: P is the standard map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lough is an Irish lake, and 'side' says the parking letter sits beside it

explanation.surface: A car park handily laid on beside a lake for stargazers to enjoy the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 4-across, whose answer is another star. 'Lakeside' has to be read as lake plus side: the lake word stands next to the parking letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough is the familiar British name for the group of seven bright stars in Ursa Major, the Big Dipper.

clue.text: Nouveau riche location second to be struck off, substandard

parts.note: par is the standard level, and the setter takes it for the level things fall below

indicators.note: struck off means removed from a list, so a letter is deleted

parts.note: a venue is a location for an event

indicators.note: second to means the second letter of the word be

explanation.surface: A description of an upstart's tatty new address: second-rate and unworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to be' points to E, the second letter of 'be', which is struck off VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone who has recently gained wealth or status without the manners to match it.

clue.text: See 29
Tyres we want him to win, we hear

parts.note: the goody is the hero of a story, the character audiences cheer for
ears are what we hear with

explanation.surface: Fans of a racing driver whose tyres they hope will carry him home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound signal but simply names the organs of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodyear is a major tyre maker, so its products are commonly known by the brand name.

clue.text: … a great one is fit to work

parts.note: to be able or fit to do something is to be able, so 'can'
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: Continuing 1-across: a big strong person is fit enough to get a job done.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis means 'one' refers back to the stars of 1-across, so 'a great one' is a great star.
explanation.definitionFit: Canopus is the second-brightest star in the night sky, so a great example of the stars just mentioned.

clue.text: Slowly, stealthily I move here, peer coyly over walls

indicators.note: over signals that the letters are turned to read the other way
the clue words wall the letters in, which are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Something sneaks along shyly peeping over the garden walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'here, peer coyly', and 'over' turns it round. Read with 'walls', the whole clue paints the plant itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A creeper is a plant that spreads slowly across walls, and also anything that moves stealthily.

clue.text: Initially, our series where you may question Vishy sacrificing a queen

definitions.text: Initially, our series where you may question
definitions.note: the initials of a long-running reader question-and-answer column in this newspaper

indicators.note: a chess sacrifice gives up a piece, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Viswanathan 'Vishy' Anand is a former world chess champion
Q is the chess abbreviation for the queen

explanation.surface: A chess column where readers query why the champion gave up his queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is initials for the Guardian's Notes and Queries column, which is why the definition begins with 'Initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes and Queries is a Guardian feature where readers send in questions for other readers to answer.

clue.text: See 26
Puzzling form on the upturn, United knocked us out

indicators.note: in a down entry an upturn reads the letters from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: KO'd is short for knocked out, so knocked us out is KO'd us
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football report: a side in good form, then United eliminated us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked us out' gives KO'D US, which 'on the upturn' turns round; U for United follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placement puzzle, a popular kind of brainteaser.

clue.text: Covering threes, when having a bet

definitions.meaning: a covering laid over a floor
bookmakers' slang for odds of three to one

explanation.surface: A punter backing a horse at threes when placing a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpet is a floor covering, and in racecourse slang it is also odds of 3-1.

clue.text: Is it reasonable not to have a second pint?

definitions.note: a question asking for the justification of something, which is what a reasoned basis supplies; noun sense taken loosely

parts.note: to ration yourself is to limit your intake, here to just one
a pint in a British pub is typically of ale or beer

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether stopping after one pint is the sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the tail as 'ration ale': limit yourself to one beer. The definition is loose: the question 'Is it reasonable?' asks for exactly the thing the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification, the thing that shows whether a course of action is sensible.

clue.text: Busy, not initially having done very much

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word not is taken
busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred about

explanation.surface: Someone frantic all day who, by evening, has achieved hardly anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal: it shuffles N (from 'not initially') with DONE. 'having' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: 'No end' is an informal idiom for a great deal, as in 'it pleased him no end'.

clue.text: Editor's leader on the reason for reciting poem

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Editor's

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so on can stand for leg

indicators.note: reciting means saying out loud, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: asking the reason for something is asking why

explanation.surface: An editor's opening article explains why a poem is being read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the on side and leg side are the same half of the field, so on gives LEG. 'reciting' turns WHY into its sound, the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, usually a lament for someone who has died.

clue.text: Nobody but Spooner could give us the language of the wisecracker!

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner is famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a wisecracker deals in quips
a jargon or language is often called a 'speak', as in management-speak

explanation.surface: Only Spooner could manage to talk in the jargon of a joker.
explanation.walkthrough: The language of a wisecracker is 'quip-speak', heard as 'quips peak'; swapping the opening sounds gives 'pips queak'. 'but' and 'of the' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an insignificant person; pipsqueak is a dismissive word for exactly such a person.

clue.text: Social climber puts about the stuff of the aesthete

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of puts are moved around

parts.note: an aesthete is devoted to art and beauty

explanation.surface: A snobbish climber affects the trappings of the cultured aesthete.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and behaves with presumption, a social climber.

clue.text: Page is upset about bloody count not opening vents

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so read backwards
not opening means without its first letter

parts.note: Count Dracula is the blood-drinking vampire

explanation.surface: A young page is horrified by the vampire count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IS into SI, which goes 'about' P; Dracula minus its opening D gives RACULA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiracula are breathing holes in insects and some fish, small openings that let air through.

clue.text: Country golf club admits women!

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the R and A, the Royal and Ancient, is the golf club at St Andrews that governs the game
W is the standard abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: A news flash: a famously male-only golf club finally lets women join.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, Scotland, long barred women members, which gives the surface its exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a nation in central-east Africa.

clue.text: Top tip for real trivia nuts, including son heading for Eggheads — he's aiming high

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the top tip of a word is its first letter, here of real

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of Eggheads

explanation.surface: Advice for quiz fanatics hoping to win on Eggheads, a BBC TV quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges R, TRIVIA, S and E; 'including' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an ambitious newcomer pushing for status, someone who sets their sights high.

clue.text: Cutter served in the US Army, 75% retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read from the end
75% means three quarters of the eight letters are kept from the front

parts.note: a GI Joe is an American soldier, so someone who served was a GI Joe

explanation.surface: A cutter (a ship) once served with the US forces before being three-quarters retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in the US Army' becomes WAS GI JOE; 75% keeps WASGIJ, and 'retired' reads it backwards. 'Cutter' suggests a boat or a person, but means the saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a saw with a fine blade for cutting curves, so a cutting tool.

clue.text: Wife in a photograph with a young rascal

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip
per means each or a, as in 'ten pounds per head'
a snap is a casual photograph
again per means a, as in 'once per day'

explanation.surface: A wife appears in a snapshot alongside a mischievous youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Both uses of 'a' are PER, meaning 'each'; 'with' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A whippersnapper is an impudent young person, the type of cheeky youngster called a rascal.

clue.text: Flying team picked up crown prince, then bragged

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a crown prince is the heir to the throne
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Someone overheard the heir to the throne and then boasted about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew is the old past tense of crow, still heard in 'the cock crew'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the team of people who operate an aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Such as divides old man and young woman, endlessly arising

definitions.text: Such as divides old man and young woman, endlessly arising

indicators.note: divides means comes between, so one piece is placed inside
in a down entry arising means going up, so read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gal is a girl or young woman
eg, short for exempli gratia, means for example or such as

explanation.surface: A wry line about a May-to-December couple, endlessly the subject of comment.
explanation.walkthrough: Pa is a familiar word for an old man or father. Read as a whole, the clue also describes what separates an old man from a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An age gap is the difference in years between two partners, what sets an older man apart from a young woman.

clue.text: Players' practice over, hitched round London's theatreland

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to get hitched is to be wed

indicators.note: over means the letters are turned back to front

parts.note: cricketers practise in the nets

explanation.surface: Actors finish rehearsal and get married near the London theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests actors, matching theatreland, but here they are cricketers, who practise in nets.
explanation.definitionFit: The West End is the central London district of theatres, the city's equivalent of Broadway.

clue.text: List issuer, sly old crook

indicators.note: crook as a verb means to bend, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Whoever issues a list is a cunning old villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a villain noun but works as the verb to bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lloyd's of London publishes Lloyd's List, the long-running shipping newspaper.

clue.text: However, American's the bluntest tool in the box?

definitions.meaning: an American word meaning at any rate or anyway

definitions.text: the bluntest tool in the box?
definitions.meaning: 'not the sharpest tool in the box' means dim, so the bluntest is the least clever, read as two words

explanation.surface: A jibe at an American as the dimmest of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is a chiefly North American adverb meaning at least or anyway, used much like however.

clue.text: Perhaps procured dress very smartly

parts.note: in a down entry TOG written upward reads GOT, which is perhaps procured

explanation.surface: Someone may have obtained a garment to dress up in style.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions, says TOG goes up, giving GOT, which the clue words define.
explanation.definitionFit: To tog up is a British informal phrasal verb meaning to put on one's best clothes.

clue.text: Feelings about individual stay in power

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: vis is Latin for force or power
to be is to stay or remain, as in 'let it be'

explanation.surface: Impressions about one person's ability to hang on to office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about individual' reads with the definition: the feelings one gets about a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibes is informal for the atmosphere or emotional signals given off by someone or something.

clue.text: See 29
Stuart guy prone to make flamboyant bid?

indicators.note: making something flamboyant rearranges it showily, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a tender is a formal bid or offer

explanation.surface: A man inclined to make showy, extravagant offers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like the definition but is fodder: GUY PRONE is rearranged by 'make flamboyant'. 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Young Pretender was Charles Edward Stuart, Bonnie Prince Charlie, who claimed the British throne in 1745.

clue.text: By-product of burning food injected to power donkey

indicators.note: injected means put inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
moke is British slang for a donkey
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Something given off when a donkey is fed to boost its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Moke is old British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat smoke is what rises from burning peat, the turf fuel that flavours some whiskies.

clue.text: See 18
Novice winked nervously at auction

indicators.note: nervously suggests jittery, twitching movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: goods being sold at auction are on the block

explanation.surface: A beginner at a sale twitches an eye to bid and is nervous about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The new kid on the block is an idiom for a newcomer still finding their feet, a novice.
